blocks.text: In Nigeria, many businesses start as sole proprietorships or partnerships. Understanding these business units is crucial for aspiring entrepreneurs.

blocks.markdown: A sole proprietorship is the simplest form of business ownership, where one individual owns and operates the business. This type of business is common in Nigeria due to its ease of establishment and minimal regulatory requirements.

blocks.title: Sole Proprietorship
blocks.text: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and managed by a single individual who is personally responsible for all its debts.

blocks.markdown:
### Features of Sole Proprietorship:
- **Single Ownership**: Only one person owns the business.
- **Unlimited Liability**: The owner is personally liable for all debts.
- **Easy to Establish**: Minimal legal requirements.

### Merits:
- Complete control over decisions.
- All profits go to the owner.

### Demerits:
- Unlimited liability can risk personal assets.
- Limited access to capital.

blocks.title: Calculating Profit in a Sole Proprietorship
blocks.prompt: If a sole proprietor earns N500,000 in revenue and incurs N300,000 in expenses, what is the profit?

steps.text: Subtract total expenses from revenue: N500,000 - N300,000.

blocks.markdown: A partnership involves two or more individuals who share ownership and management of a business. It is essential for partners to have a partnership deed, which outlines the terms of their agreement.

blocks.title: Partnership
blocks.text: A partnership is a business arrangement where two or more individuals share ownership, responsibilities, and profits.

blocks.markdown:
### Features of a Partnership:
- **Shared Ownership**: Multiple individuals own the business.
- **Partnership Deed**: A legal document that defines the terms of the partnership.

### Contents of a Partnership Deed:
- Names of partners
- Business name and purpose
- Profit-sharing ratio
- Responsibilities of each partner
- Duration of the partnership.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When discussing business units, focus on the implications of unlimited liability in sole proprietorships and partnerships, as it is a common exam question.

points: Sole proprietorships are owned by one individual with unlimited liability.
Partnerships involve two or more individuals and require a partnership deed.
